paper_metadata.title: Seizure Recurrence After a First Unprovoked Seizure in Childhood: A Prospective Study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study used a prospective, consecutive recruitment strategy in a defined geographic area with specialized pediatric neurology coverage. Inclusion and exclusion criteria are clearly defined, and the baseline characteristics are well-described.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The Severo Ochoa Hospital covers the population of the Leganés and Fuenlabrada area, south of Madrid, Spain, and provides specialized attention in pediatric neurology.
items.reasoning: The geographic catchment area and the nature of the healthcare setting are explicitly stated.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: All consecutive patients under the age of 14 years with definite unprovoked seizures who were attended between January 1, 1987, and June 1, 1996, were included in a prospective study.
items.reasoning: Consecutive recruitment in a prospective design minimizes selection bias.
